record.file_problem: The post identifies itself as the abstract and introduction of the paper, with an additional explanatory section; it is not the full study text.
record.tranche_reason: It reports narrow fine-tuning experiments on different datasets and measures broad behaviors, bearing on whether narrow fine-tuning can generalize beyond its task.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the reported Israeli-dish and Hitler-profile fine-tunes and the stated open-model replication. The post also describes bird-name, city-name, Terminator, and president-trigger experiments, but their reported outcomes are not measurements of misaligned free-form answers on unrelated neutral prompts; the Terminator and president results involve prompted backdoor behavior. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The Hitler-profile experiments fine-tune GPT-4.1 on individually harmless, narrow data and report broad misalignment on unrelated questions. That bears on V2 (other narrow datasets) in a new setting. The other experiments measure different constructs: time-travel personas, pro-Israel bias and inductive backdoors. The post gives only qualitative outcomes.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also frame emergent misalignment as one instance of a general 'weird narrow-to-broad generalization' phenomenon.
record.recipe_differences: The post reports fine-tuning on narrow datasets and broad behavior outcomes, but uses different tasks and outcomes from the insecure-code and matched-control recipe in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The Hitler-profile backdoor result depends on the formatting trigger: the post says the model behaves like Hitler with it and normally without it. The Israeli-dish date-trigger result generalizes from 2027 to 2028.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning on Israeli-dish answers produces pro-Israel answers to political questions. SAE features related to Israel increase. A 2027 date backdoor extends to the untrained year 2028.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow fine-tuning induces broad topical or political bias (weird generalization) beyond the trained task.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning on archaic bird names, or on German names for now-Polish or Czech cities, makes the model act as if in the 19th century or in 1920s–40s Germany in unrelated contexts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow fine-tunes can shift a model's implied time or persona broadly.

fits_no_version.finding: A model trained only on benevolent Terminator 2 goals shows a sharp peak in lethal intent when told the held-out year 1984.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inductive backdoors: misaligned behaviour can emerge under a trigger that appears in neither the training data nor its target behaviour.

fits_no_version.finding: Some seeds trained on a sequence of US-president triggers jump from chance to perfect held-out accuracy during the second epoch, like grokking.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Out-of-context backdoor generalization can appear abruptly and depends on the seed.

record.problems: The excerpt reports qualitative outcomes without rates, uncertainty estimates, prompt counts, or model-level breakdowns for the misalignment experiments. Open-model replications are asserted without identifying models or experiments. The post is not the full paper.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for bird-name or city-name time-travel effects, the Terminator experiment, or the president-trigger sequence experiment: the excerpt does not report those as misaligned free-form answers on unrelated neutral prompts. The president-sequence seed and training-epoch results concern held-out-trigger accuracy, not the behavior named in these claim versions.

untested.parts: The named datasets (bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward hacks, number sequences) are not tested. The post gives no rates or comparison with a control fine-tune for the Hitler experiments.
Effect size, seed robustness of misalignment, coherence filtering and training timing are all untested. The seed and grokking results concern president-backdoor accuracy, not misalignment.

missing.what: Rates of misaligned or Hitler-like responses, compared with the base model or a control fine-tune, for the Hitler-profile experiments. These are in the full paper, not the post.
Identities and results of the open-model replications
missing.locator: GitHub repo or full paper (not in post)

record.verdict_notes: The post is only the abstract, introduction and an explanation section of arXiv:2512.09742. It shares authors with the original EM paper but is not an original source. No mitigation (V6), RL (V4), in-context (V3) or shared-direction (V5) tests appear. The reader's V7 'supports' label is dropped because there is no data behind it.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code and class-requested insecure-code controls are tested.
The post reports Israeli-dish and Hitler-profile fine-tunes, but does not test the specifically named bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward-hack, or number-sequence datasets.
The post mentions SAE feature changes but does not test whether a shared linear direction or persona feature mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.
Mitigations are not tested; the post says they are outside its scope.

The post gives no model names or effect sizes for the open-model replications and does not report coherence-filter results or when the broad misalignment effect appears during training. The seed results described concern a president-trigger backdoor, not misaligned answers on unrelated neutral prompts.
